title: Keser as the middle: the Essence's delight in every sefira, Atik and Arich, and Atik Yomin
overview:
Chapter 24 gives the *nimshal* of everything said about will and delight: how it applies to *Keser*. The simple delight of the Essence, *sha'ashuei hamelech b'atzmuso*, is G-d's complete self-expression before the *tzimtzum*, and the ten essential *sefiros* are all part of it; yet the Essence itself is removed even from that and only shines through delight. That desire to reveal Himself comes down through the *ratzon kadum* to the end of everything, like the delight in winning that reaches every move and every t-shirt.

*Atik* and *Arich*, delight and will, are one essence, enclothed in every *sefira* as its existence and encompassing all of them, like oil and like water poured into ten pits. *Atik* still counts as the world of the *Ein Sof*, G-d's free choice; *Arich* is the head of the emanated, so *Keser* is the middle. In detail, *Atik*'s kindness is in the *gulgalta*, so a father at his son's wedding grants anything, and its *gevura* in the hidden wisdom, which is why the Torah has so many exact laws. Above all, *Atik Yomin* is the Essence's eternity shining into time and making it infinite, as a line holds infinite points.

sections.title: The nimshal: everything is from the simple delight, yet the Essence is beyond even delight
sections.summary: The *Keser* of G-d is the *nimshal* of all that was said about will and delight: before the *tzimtzum* there is the simple delight of the Essence, *sha'ashuei hamelech b'atzmuso*, and the ten essential *sefiros* are all its self-expression. Yet the Essence itself is removed even from that; it only shines through delight, which is why nothing in the *hishtalshelus* is higher than pleasure.

איך שבחינת עצמות התענוג הפשוט שבעצמות אור אין סוף קודם הצמצום,
הוא הנקרא שעשועי המלך בעצמותו,
phrases.en: called *sha'ashuei hamelech b'atzmuso*: the *taanug* in Himself,

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת אין סוף ממש
phrases.en: which is completely unlimited.

phrases.he: וגם בעשר ספירות העצמיים שהוא כתר ועד מלכות דאין סוף, הכל מבחינת העונג הפשוט שבעצמותו
phrases.en: And also the *yud sefiros atzmiyim* are all part of the *taanug pashut sheb'atzmuso*. They're all like a self-expression.

blocks.text: Now he gives the *nimshal* (what an analogy stands for) of all that was said about *ratzon* (will) and *taanug* (delight): how it applies to *Keser* (crown), to the simple *taanug* called *sha'ashuei hamelech b'atzmuso* (the King's delight in Himself). The real meaning of *taanug* is when something reflects back on the *etzem* (essence).

*Ratzon* is where the *etzem* lowers itself to relate and invests itself in something with a particular form: either a part of its own *etzem*, or something outside it, a *ratzon murkav* (a composite will). When that thing reflects back on it, that is *taanug*: from a part of its *etzem*, a *taanug atzmi* (an essential delight); from outside it, a *taanug murkav*.

So too *ratzon* above is G-d's ability to lower Himself, to have something express Him. Either it is part of the *etzem*, like the ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes), a *mi'ut* (a lessening) to reveal Himself in a limited way; or it is outside His *etzem*: mainly the particulars of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya* (the three lower worlds), even the *kelim* (vessels) of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation).

In the *etzem* it is called **sha'ashuei hamelech b'atzmuso: the taanug in Himself**, **completely unlimited**. Before the *tzimtzum* (contraction), the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light) is G-d's complete expression of Himself: the whole *etzem taanug*, the whole essential self-expression, comes out there. **And also the yud sefiros atzmiyim** (the ten essential *sefiros*) **are all part of the taanug pashut sheb'atzmuso**, the simple delight in His essence. **They're all like a self-expression.**

phrases.he: על דרך משל שגם החסד העצמי שבנפש, עיקר קיומו העונג כו'
phrases.en: just like we see how the main *kiyum* of the *chesed* in a person is the fact that he enjoys it,

blocks.title: Kindness lives on its enjoyment
blocks.text: **Just like we see how the main kiyum** (what keeps it in existence) **of the chesed** (kindness) **in a person is the fact that he enjoys it**, so too G-d limits Himself to all these things because they are a way to express Himself: there is *taanug* in it.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה באמת הרי עצמות אור אין סוף מובדל גם מבחינת תענוג פשוט
phrases.en: But still the real *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* is removed even from this thing of a *taanug pashut*,

phrases.he: רק שנמשך ומאיר בבחינת העונג,
phrases.en: just that it comes into the *inyan* of pleasure,

phrases.he: כמו שעצמות הנפש תומשך אחר העונג כו'
phrases.en: like the soul is drawn after other things through *taanug*.

blocks.text: **But still the real Atzmus Or Ein Sof** (the Essence of the infinite light) **is removed even from this thing of a taanug pashut**, **just that it comes into the inyan of pleasure**, as the essence of the soul is drawn after pleasure. All of these are still *gilu'im* (revelations).

We cannot say that G-d is this all-encompassing ability for *gilu'im*, as if He were a *Maor* (the source of light); it is just that He can also do this. And this is the connection: **like the soul is drawn after other things through taanug**, so G-d connects with other things through what we call *or*, light, a revelation of Himself.

phrases.he: ולזה אמר אין לך למעלה מן העונג כו'
phrases.en: That's why the early *mekubalim* said that there's nothing higher than pleasure.

blocks.text: **That's why the early mekubalim** (Kabbalists) **said that there's nothing higher than pleasure**: nothing we can relate to, nothing in the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent), is higher. This is the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*. Beyond it is just the *etzem*, which has nothing to do with revelation; it is not a level in the *hishtalshelus* that you could call *maala u'mata*, higher and lower.

sections.title: The desire for kindness comes down, through the ratzon kadum, to the end of everything
sections.summary: G-d's *chafetz chesed*, His desire to reveal Himself as a creator, has a simple delight in it, and so it comes down to a separate thing: through the *ratzon kadum* after the *tzimtzum*, the whole *hishtalshelus*, down to the lowest *sefiros* of *Atzilus* that feed the world and run the weather. Like the delight in winning, which reaches every move, the victory dance and all the paraphernalia.

phrases.he: וכמו בבחינת חפץ חסד שבעצמות,
phrases.en: For example, the *inyan* of the *chafetz chesed* in the *Atzmus*: G-d's ability, or His desire, to express Himself,

phrases.he: שיש בו תענוג הפשוט
phrases.en: which has a *taanug pashut*.

phrases.he: הוא נמשך ומאיר בתוספת אור עד שיורד ובא גם בדבר נבדל
phrases.en: So it came down to even come to something *nivdal*,

blocks.text: For example, the *chafetz chesed* (the desire for kindness) in the *Atzmus*, G-d's desire to reveal Himself as a creator, **has a taanug pashut**: a unique revelation of G-d is in it. Just as a person goes after *taanug*, so does Hashem; that is the reason for the desire to reveal it, **so it came down to even come to something nivdal** (separate).

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת תענוג והרצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל
שאחר הצמצום, להיות מקור להשתלשלות דאבי''ע
phrases.en: to come after *tzimtzum* and to express this thing through actually creating our world, which is the whole *hishtalshelus*

phrases.he: עד שיורד ונמשך בסיום הכל,
phrases.en: until it comes all the way down

phrases.he: והוא גם בפרט דעשר ספירות היותר אחרון שבאצילות
phrases.en: And this is so even of the lowest thing in *Atzilus*, the lowest *sefiros*,

blocks.text: It comes as *taanug* and the *ratzon kadum* (the primordial will), **to come after tzimtzum and to express this thing through actually creating our world, which is the whole hishtalshelus**, more and more until it comes *mamash* (actually) to the world as we have it. The *ratzon kadum* is just to create a world that is separate.

**Until it comes all the way down**, to create the world as it is now. **And this is so even of the lowest thing in Atzilus, the lowest sefiros**: *Nehi* (*netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*), how Hashem acts in a world already created and separate, giving *mazon* (sustenance) or affecting the weather. Even that comes from the *taanug pashut*, because there is a unique revelation of G-d in it.

phrases.he: על דרך משל הנזכר לעיל בעונג הנמצא לקיום מדת הניצוח וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: Just like in a person, what keeps up his interest in winning

blocks.title: The victory dance
blocks.text: **Just like in a person, what keeps up his interest in winning** and all the little things that come with it, every bit of practice, every move, and after he wins the whole victory dance: all these *pratim* (details) come from his *taanug* in *nitzuach* (victory). It spreads into all of them, until he gets into all the paraphernalia. That is the *orech hadaas* (the length of *daas*).

blocks.title: The fan and the team t-shirt
blocks.text: "Yeah, that's an *orech hadaas*." People get so into something that they want many *asiyos* (deeds) and all the paraphernalia. Partly it is *nitzuach*, partly wanting to belong, and not *davka* (specifically) sports: there is a special thrill in winning, and by connecting to the team they get the thrill that their team won. The more their *daas* (the mind's bond with what it understands) is connected, the more they want to know everything about it and have the t-shirt, "and whatever, all the different things."
blocks.outOfPlace: At the end of class 05, after he has read line 14, he comes back to the length of daas in the mashal of line 12, apparently answering a question the recording does not catch.

blocks.title: A fan of G-d
blocks.text: Chapter one, which we will soon reach, says that with *daas* in holiness a person has to become like a fan of G-d. That is *Torah lishma* (for its own sake): learning things that may never come up. It is not practical; you love G-d so much that you want to know everything about Him, what He wants. So all of Torah becomes precious, and you want *tashmishei kedusha* (articles used for holiness) very nice, a *hiddur mitzva* (beautifying a commandment): a nice menorah, a nice esrog, your connection brought down into tangible expressions. Everything can be from the side of *kelipa* (lit. husk; what conceals G-dliness) or of *kedusha* (holiness).

sections.title: Atik and Arich, delight and will, are one essence: inside every sefira and encompassing them all
sections.summary: *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* are the delight and the will, one essence, and they are enclothed in every *sefira* down to its smallest detail as its existence. Yet the *Keser* also encompasses them all: like oil it stays above and permeates everything, like water poured into ten pits, like G-d putting on different garments.

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב בעץ חיים, דעתיק יומין ואריך אנפין, שהוא התענוג והרצון, שמהות אחד הם, (ונקרא ג' רישין דמתגלפין דא לגו מן דא כו' ולפעמים זה פנימי
כו' כנזכר לעיל(ואין זה
בלא זה
מלובש תוך כל ספירה וספירה בפרטי פרטות,
phrases.en: the *taanug* and the *ratzon*, which is *Atik* and *Arich*, goes into every single *sefira*, including all of its details, of how they subdivide,

phrases.he: שבלעדו אין לו קיום כלל כנזכר לעיל באריכות
phrases.en: and without it there's no *kiyum* at all,

blocks.text: As *Etz Chaim* says, *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* (lit. the Ancient of Days and the long countenance) are the *taanug* and the *ratzon*, one essence, neither without the other. So **the taanug and the ratzon, which is Atik and Arich, goes into every single sefira, including all of its details, of how they subdivide**, how one is enclothed in another, every combination that creates each thing.

Each one has a unique expression of G-dliness, its motivation and its real *kiyum*, and G-d chose which to connect Himself to. As we said, you can have a *taanug* in something, but if you do not want it you will not have it. So G-d has to want to, lowering Himself to choose; without that there is no *taanug* in it.

blocks.title: Moral because G-d commanded it?
blocks.text:
Last time he mentioned the ancient philosophical question: is morality moral because G-d commanded it, or did He command it because it is moral? That is exactly the question of which comes first, *Atik* or *Arich*. The answer: they are synonymous, so you can never say which comes first; in the *etzem* they are one thing.

There is a unique *taanug* in morality, but had G-d not chosen it, He could have chosen the unique *taanug* in something else; from that side His *ratzon* comes first. On the other hand, He chose it because it was the unique thing He wanted to reveal. So what makes it good is the choice, and yet Hashem wanted it *davka* for its virtues.
So these are enclothed in everything, **and without it there's no kiyum at all**, as explained above at length.

phrases.he: וגם הוא מקיף את כולם
phrases.en: but on the other hand, it's also *makif* all of them.

blocks.text: **But on the other hand, it's also makif** (encompassing) **all of them.** Each thing has a unique *taanug* and *ratzon* that makes it what it is, but the *etzem taanug* and *ratzon* is higher than all of them, just for Himself; it does not matter to it whether it is this way or that.

Once it chooses, it is connected to one form, as was learned in *Tarsach* (5668). The real *ratzon* is to be happy; a person connects that to money, food, *kavod* (honor), and can get very connected to one of them. But those are only the *middos* (attributes) of the *ratzon*. The *etzem ratzon* and *taanug* is just expressing himself, feeling his vitality: it is all the same to it, it could pick something else, but once it picks, it puts itself into it.

blocks.title: Choosing one path in life
blocks.text: Like choosing what path to take in life, what to specialize in: from the side of your *etzem* you could do anything, but to actually do anything, *b'poel mamash*, you have to pick one thing.

blocks.title: Oil stays apart and permeates
blocks.text: So the *Keser* is *makif* all the *sefiros*: the real *etzem* of all of them is one thing, higher than any of them, a revelation of G-d. And therefore it is *mefa'pe'a*, it spreads into everything, like oil, which stays separate from everything and spreads into everything: "This does not mix with anything, and this permeates everything." The *Keser* is higher than everything, and yet spreads into each thing individually.

This is why it says that *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching) is a new revelation of *Keser*, a new light from *Keser*, really the *ra'ava d'chol ra'avin* (the will of all wills): its point is to reveal this *etzem* of everything, how everything is really a revelation of G-d. So *Kuntres Inyana shel Toras HaChassidus* explains both things, that it is higher than everything and that it comes into everything, and compares it to oil.

phrases.he: )וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר במשל עשר חפירות זה אחר זה שהראשונה נמשכת בתוך כל חפירה וחפירה כו'
phrases.en: like it's explained elsewhere about a *mashal* of ten pits, one after the other, like an ice cube tray: if you pour water into the first one, it will fill it up, and then it will overflow into the second, then into the third, and then it will fill them all up.

phrases.he: וכך אמר בזהר עבד מנא רברבא וקארי בה גרמיה חכים כו'
phrases.en: Hashem made many garments, and He called them wisdom and understanding,

phrases.he: וכן מה שכתוב אפיק עשר תיקונין וקרינן לון עשר ספירות כו׳)
phrases.en: Hashem made ten garments, *tikunin* means garments, and He called them ten *sefiros*.

blocks.title: Ten pits, like an ice cube tray
blocks.text: **Like it's explained elsewhere about a mashal of ten pits, one after the other, like an ice cube tray: if you pour water into the first one, it will fill it up, and then it will overflow into the second, then into the third**, until all are full. "I think" the water is the *Keser*, the *ratzon* and *taanug*: it pours first into *chachma* (wisdom), overflows into *bina* (understanding), and so into all of them.

blocks.title: Water takes the shape of the vessel
blocks.text: It goes into each one and fits it, as water takes the shape of the *kli* (vessel), yet the water is the same in all of them and not limited to any *kli*. If each had a different color it would look different; they give all these *meshalim* (analogies), but the *etzem or* is the same.

So the *Zohar* says: **Hashem made many garments, and He called them wisdom and understanding.** The ten *sefiros* are *levushim* (garments): the *etzem* is the same in each, and its external form differs by the *kli*. It is really G-d, putting on different garments.

blocks.title: A sage at Sinai, a warrior at the Sea
blocks.text: He dresses up and acts out the role of a wise person: at *Matan Torah* (the giving of the Torah) they saw Him as a sage with a long white beard, at *Krias Yam Suf* (the splitting of the Sea) as a young warrior. One time He put on the clothes of *netzach* (victory), the other time of *chachma*, "but it's the same *Aibershter*" (the One Above).
And what it says, "He brought out ten *tikunin* and called them ten *sefiros*", means the same thing: **Hashem made ten garments, tikunin means garments, and He called them ten sefiros.**

sections.title: Keser as the middle: Atik is still the world of the Infinite, Arich is the head of what is emanated
sections.summary: *Atik Yomin* still counts as the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*, because everything down to *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* is still G-d's free choice, like a drawing of a tree that is still infinite. *Arich Anpin*, the will that comes from the delight to make a world, is already the head of the emanated. So *Keser* is the *memutza*: the end of the Essence and the head of the *ne'etzalim*, which are separate from the Essence the way a kind man's coats are separate from his kindness.

phrases.he: להיות כי בחינת עתיק יומין נחשב מסוף עולם האין סוף עדיין
phrases.en: that *Atik* is considered the end of the *Ein Sof* still.

phrases.he: לפי שעולם האין סוף נחשב עד בחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון, שהוא בחינת אותיות וסוף מעשה שעלה במחשבה ורצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: Because **Atik is considered the end of the Ein Sof still.** The *olam ha'Ein Sof* (the world of the Infinite) means it is still a free *bechira* (choice). So it is counted until *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* (lit. primordial man; the first world), sometimes down to *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, sometimes even in the *kelim* of *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*: "even if I'll give you just two choices, it's still an expression of your *bechira*."

blocks.title: Draw me a tree
blocks.text: "I'm going to give you a pen and a paper, and I want you to make me a picture of a tree." Severe limitations, yet the possibilities are infinite. So though G-d chose to reveal Himself in a limited way, through *Adam Kadmon*, only through the ten *sefiros*, the way He can use them is still infinite: it is still the world of the *Ein Sof*, and sometimes even what comes after it.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת אחרונה שבעצמות שנעשה כתר דעתיק יומין,
שזהו בחינת גלוי אור העונג מהעלם העונג ורצון קדום הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: This is the *gilui* of the *etzem taanug*, which was in the *ratzon kadum*,

phrases.he: על כן גם כתר דעתיק יומין וחכמה ובינה ומדות שבו, הכל נחשב מסוף עולם האין סוף
phrases.en: Therefore *Atik* is still considered the end of the world of *Ein Sof*.

blocks.text:
It is the last level of the Essence, which becomes the *Keser* of *Atik Yomin*. Hashem chose to reveal Himself through this form, in the *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon*; nothing was imposed on Him, so it is *Ein Sof*, and the *taanug* that comes through it is still a direct revelation of His *etzem*, put into it *mamash*.

**This is the gilui of the etzem taanug, which was in the ratzon kadum**, to reveal Himself by creating a world in this form. **Therefore Atik is still considered the end of the world of Ein Sof**, with its *Keser*, *chachma*, *bina* and *middos*.

phrases.he: אבל בחינת אריך אנפין שהוא בחינת גלוי הרצון שבא מחמת העונג להיותו נמשך ובא להתפשט למטה כו', הוא הנקרא ראש ושרש הנאצלים, שהן עשר ספירות דאצילות בכלל ובפרט

blocks.text: But *Arich Anpin*, the revelation of the will that comes because of the delight, to spread below, is called the head and root of the *ne'etzalim* (what is emanated). Because Hashem wants to reveal Himself this way, He wants to create such a world and do such and such: that is already outside relative to the *etzem taanug*, just the means to the end. These are the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, in general and in detail.

phrases.he: ולזה נקרא בחינת הכתר בכלל בחינת ממוצע,
phrases.en: This is why *Keser* in general is called a *memutza*,

phrases.he: שיש בו מבחינת אחרונה שבעצמות, והוא ראש לנאצלים
phrases.en: It has both the end of the *Atzmus*, and it's also the beginning of the *ne'etzalim*.

blocks.text: **This is why Keser in general is called a memutza** (a middle). **It has both the end of the Atzmus, and it's also the beginning of the ne'etzalim.**

phrases.he: כי אורות הנאצלים שהן בחינת גילוי ההעלם, הרי הן בבחינת נבדל מן העצמות כנזכר לעיל (באות י''ב) וכמו על דרך משל המדות חסד וגבורה בדבר נבדל, שבאין מכח המדות חסד וגבורה שבעצם כו'

blocks.title: The nice guy's coats
blocks.text: The lights of the *ne'etzalim*, a *gilui ha'helem* (revelation of what is hidden), are separate from the Essence. ("The *os* is supposed to be a *tes*.") As we said: a person's essential choice to be a nice guy comes from his *etzem*. But that in such a circumstance, in such a society, kindness means giving *tzedaka* (charity), coats or shoes, is circumstantial, not really his choice. In that sense it is already something separate.

Yet sometimes it says that even the end of *Atzilus* is part of the *Ein Sof*, because even within these things there are still choices: exactly how to do it, and how much to express each of the *middos*.

As with *chesed* and *gevura* (might, restraint) in a separate thing, which come from the *chesed* and *gevura* in the essence. Choosing to be nice is a person's self-expression, but the particular thing he did is not an expression of the *etzem*: from what comes out of it you could get the wrong idea, unless you understand what he means by it.

blocks.title: Masked men at the table
blocks.text: As the Rebbe likes to bring down: you see people strapping somebody down to a table and masked men cutting him up. You would think they are "terrible, horrible people that are torturing this poor guy," and really they are surgeons trying to save his life. What comes out is already separate: unless you connect it back to what they mean, you will not see the *etzem* there. Once you do, the revelation comes all the way down.

That is really the main point of going through the *shorashim* (roots): to keep seeing it. Once you understand the language, how these levels connect, you see how the *etzem or* comes over to the next level, and the next level.

sections.title: The delight enclothed in everything is its existence; without it, a thing is neglected
sections.summary: The delight and will that come from the Essence are enclothed in everything, as what keeps it in existence every moment, because G-d wants to reveal Himself through it. Delight means the soul is expressed through a thing; so *kelipa*, which opposes it, has no real existence, and even a king would drop his kingship if he took no pleasure in it.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה בחינת התענוג והרצון שבא מן העצמות, הוא מלובש תוך כל, להיות קיומם תמיד כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: But nevertheless, this *taanug* and *ratzon* that comes from the *etzem* goes into every single little thing that he's choosing what he wants to do.

phrases.he: מפני ששרש זה התענוג והרצון, בעצמות אור אין סוף שנקרא שעשועי המלך בעצמו כו'

blocks.text: **But nevertheless, this taanug and ratzon that comes from the etzem goes into every single little thing that he's choosing what he wants to do.** So everything is a revelation of his *etzem*: what motivates that attribute is that he wants to express himself as that kind of person.

Because the root of this *taanug* and *ratzon* is in the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*, called *sha'ashuei hamelech b'atzmo*. Now the *nimshal*: the world is the way it is, and G-d is in every single thing that happens, because Hashem wants to reveal that aspect of His *etzem* through that thing. If we learn to see it, we will understand what He reveals; sometimes we get the wrong idea and do not appreciate it.

phrases.he: וכמשל הנפש שנמשך אחר כל עונג כו',
phrases.en: Like the soul that goes after every pleasure,

phrases.he: שמזה ראיה שהעונג ממלא אורה כו'
phrases.en: From this we see that the *taanug* fills up the light of the soul,

phrases.he: אם כן גם מזה עצמו הוא הטעם שהעונג פרטי שבכל פרט מן האורות, הוא עיקר קיומו כו'
phrases.en: That's why the *taanug* in each thing, that is really the *etzem* of that thing,

blocks.text: **Like the soul that goes after every pleasure. From this we see that the taanug fills up the light of the soul**: the *etzem* expresses itself through the thing. That is what *taanug* means, so the more *taanug* it gets in something, the more it connects to it, expressing more of itself there.

**That's why the taanug in each thing, that is really the etzem of that thing**: it is what the soul gets out of it. "Well, what do I get out of it? Why do I want to do it?" So above: what keeps everything existing every moment is G-d's *taanug* in it, that it somehow reveals G-dliness. That is why *kelipa* is a nonentity, like a shadow, with no real *metzius* (existence): what is opposite to His *ratzon* and *taanug* has none.

blocks.question: What of people who delight in what is bad?
blocks.text: "They're feeling a *taanug*, but the question is what are they feeling a *taanug* from?" Sometimes it is a good *taanug* in G-dliness that they mess up, taking one little thing out of context, as if you separated the guy's kindness from his *etzem*; then it becomes bad. The excitement is really good, but they are sold something false: if you do this and this, let's say, you will win. They are all excited, and then it is not true. Their real *ratzon*, the real *taanug* they are looking for, is not bad; just the way it comes out is bad.

phrases.he: עד גם בבחינת המלכות שהוא ההתנשאות
phrases.en: Even, same thing, even with *Malchus*, to be a king,

phrases.he: לולי התענוג שבו אין לו קיום כו'
phrases.en: if there wouldn't be a *taanug* in being king, you wouldn't want to do it.

phrases.he: והעדר אור העונג הוא בחינת העדר אור מציאותם כו'
phrases.en: But now if you'll have a want of pleasure in it, then he'll neglect it and pull away from it

phrases.he: ודי למבין.
וכל זה דרך כלל
phrases.en: But that's only in general.

blocks.text: So **even with Malchus** (kingship), **to be a king: if there wouldn't be a taanug in being king, you wouldn't want to do it.** **But now if you'll have a want of pleasure in it, then he'll neglect it and pull away from it** and get involved in other things. That is the general picture of *Atik* and *Arich* and the *sefiros*; **but that's only in general**, and now he gives more detail.

sections.title: In detail: only the three heads of Atik count as the Essence; its kindness opens the will
sections.summary: In detail, only the three heads of *Atik* belong to the Essence; its seven lower attributes are enclothed in *Arich*, its kindness in the *gulgalta* and its *gevura* in the *mocha stima'a*. The will is born from the attributes of the delight: a father at his son's wedding, flooded with delight, will grant anything and turn even judgment into kindness, because it reaches the point of will above the hidden reason.

phrases.he: אבל דרך פרט, הנה רק בחינת ג׳ ראשין דעתיק יומין נחשב מבחינת העצמות
phrases.en: In particular, only the *Keser*, *chachma*, *bina* of *Atik* is considered part of the *etzem*,

phrases.he: אבל ז׳ תחתונים שבו מלובש בגלגלתא דאריך אנפין
phrases.en: but the seven *middos* of *Atik* are enclothed into *Arich* already.

phrases.he: חסד דעתיק יומין בגלגלתא
phrases.en: The *chesed* of *Atik* goes into the skull, the *Keser* of *Arich*,

phrases.he: וגבורה במוחא סתימאה כו'
phrases.en: and *gevura* goes into the *mocha stima'a*, the *chachma* of *Arich*,

blocks.text: **In particular, only the Keser, chachma, bina of Atik is considered part of the etzem**, the *gimmel reishin* (the three heads); that is like the *Reisha d'lo isyada* (the head that is not known). **But the seven middos of Atik are enclothed into Arich already.**

In order, **the chesed of Atik goes into the skull, the Keser of Arich, and gevura goes into the mocha stima'a** (the hidden brain), **the chachma of Arich**, and *tiferes* (beauty) into *bina* of *Arich*. *Netzach* and *hod* get split into inner and outer sides: "Forget exactly the order." These are the seven *tikunim* of the *gulgalta* (the skull), from *chesed* through *Malchus* of *Atik*; the thirteen *tikunim* of the *dikna* (the beard) are those of *Arich*.

phrases.he: כידוע, להיות כי התהוות עיקר הרצון מן התענוג, הוא רק מבחינת המדות שבתענוג
phrases.en: The *ratzon* comes *davka* from the *middos* of the *taanug*.

phrases.he: כמו מן החסד שבתענוג

blocks.text: As is known, the will comes from the delight only through the attributes in the delight: **the ratzon comes davka from the middos of the taanug.** The *ratzon* is a means to the end: since you want a *taanug* in such and such a form, you need such and such a *ratzon*. For example, from the *chesed* in the *taanug*.

phrases.he: על דרך משל, כאשר אדם בעונג בשמחת חתונת בנו וכהאי גוונא,
phrases.en: Like for example if a person's at a wedding, at their son's wedding,

phrases.he: אז יטיב רב חסדו לכל
מצד התענוג שמרומם את נפשו
phrases.en: because they get such a big *taanug*,

phrases.he: (מטעם הנזכר לעיל)

blocks.title: At his son's wedding
blocks.text: **Like for example if a person's at a wedding, at their son's wedding**: **because they get such a big taanug**, you can get them to say yes to anything. The *chesed* of *taanug* is a big felt pleasure (its *gevura* is like pain), and that creates the *etzem ratzon*: they just want to express themselves, let the world know, so they will do anything; they do not care what it is.

phrases.he: ואז יפעלו ממנו כל רצון
phrases.en: then you can get them to want anything,

phrases.he: דהיינו להפוך גם מרצון של דין לחסד
phrases.en: So even if he was before angry at somebody or whatever, you can turn it over,

phrases.he: שזה תלוי בבחינת נקודת הרצון שלמעלה מטעם כמוס לרצון,
phrases.en: this is connecting to *etzem ratzon*, the *nekuda* which is higher than the reason for *ratzon*.

phrases.he: שמחלק לחסד וגבורה, חסד ודין כו'

blocks.text: **Then you can get them to want anything**, even turning a will of judgment into kindness: **so even if he was before angry at somebody or whatever, you can turn it over**, as kings would often pardon people at their son's wedding.

Because **this is connecting to etzem ratzon, the nekuda** (point) **which is higher than the reason for ratzon.** The *ta'am kamus* (the hidden reason) of the will wants a *taanug davka* in a certain form. Here he does not care which: he feels such a big *hispashtus* (spreading forth) of his existence that he needs *kelim* to fill it, any *kelim*. Normally he limits himself by the reason that divides into *chesed* and *din* (judgement), a *ratzon murkav* that wants some things and not others. "But here it's an *etzem* thing."

As *Yafa Sha'ah Achas* says about the head: when a *taanug* comes through so much that it goes over the whole head, it does not matter; he wants everything. Normally it only drips down a little, so he wants only certain things that are easy to get *taanug* from, according to his *kelim*.

phrases.he: וזהו דוגמא להבין איך שבחינת חסד דעתיק יומין מלובש בגלגלתא כו'
phrases.en: This is the way that the *chesed* of *Atik* is *meluvash* in the *gulgalta*,

blocks.text: And this is the likeness by which to understand how **the chesed of Atik is meluvash** (enclothed) **in the gulgalta**: in other words, it goes into this liquid: that is the *chesed* of *Atik*.

sections.title: Gevura in the hidden wisdom: why chachma is judgment, and why the Torah has many laws
sections.summary: The *gevura* of *Atik*, judgment and the opposite of delight, is enclothed in the *mocha stima'a*, the hidden reason of the will: the delight only drips through in certain places, so the will is exacting, this way and not another. That is why the early Kabbalists said *chachma* is judgment, and why the Torah, from the higher wisdom, has so many exact laws.

phrases.he: ובחינת גבורה, שהוא בחינת הדין, בהיפך לעונג,
phrases.en: The *gevura*, which is the *din*, which means from pain, the opposite of the *oneg*,

phrases.he: הוא מלובש בחכמה סתימאה דאריך אנפין, שהוא טעם כמוס לרצון
שזהו לדקדק ברצון, שיהיה באופן זה דוקא ולא באופן אחר כו'

blocks.text: The skull is from the *chesed* of *Atik*; the liquid is the *mocha stima'a*, and the skull forces it down everywhere in the head. The *kruma* (the membrane), from *tiferes* of *Atik*, lets it out more in some places and less in others: the *bina* of *Arich*, which associates the *taanug* with certain things. The *gevura* lets it drip only a little through the hairs: the *mocha stima'a* of *Arich Anpin*, the *ta'am kamus* of the will, which comes to pain.

**The gevura, which is the din, which means from pain, the opposite of the oneg** (delight), is enclothed in the *mocha stima'a* of *Arich Anpin* and makes a *ta'am kamus*: the will is exacting, *davka* this way and not another. Since it drips only in a few places and in a limited way, he gets *taanug* only in a certain form, so he wants only certain things; his *ratzon* gets a direction.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב בספרי הקבלה שהראשונים גזרו אומר על החכמה שהיא בבחינת דין
phrases.en: That's why they said the *chachma* is on the side of *din*,

phrases.he: שכאשר הרצון בא על פי חיוב החכמה, בא בדקדוק וצמצום, כך ולא כך

blocks.text: The early books of Kabbala declared that *chachma* is *din*. **That's why they said the chachma is on the side of din**: it limits the *ratzon* to one form, *davka*, and when the will comes by the necessity of *chachma*, it comes exacting and limited, this way and not that. Since he gets pain from certain things, it becomes nitpicky: he goes around what is painful and involves himself only with what is pleasurable.

phrases.he: ועל כן על פי משפט התורה, דאורייתא מחכמה עילאה כו',
phrases.en: and this is why the Torah, which comes from *chachma ila'a*,

phrases.he: יש דינים רבים
phrases.en: There's a lot of *dinim*.

blocks.text: **And this is why the Torah, which comes from chachma ila'a** (the higher wisdom), has many laws: **there's a lot of dinim.** Most *mitzvos* (commandments) are *lo sa'aseh*, do nots, and even the *asei*'s are exacting, *davka* this way. *Tefillin* has to be exactly right to be kosher, "or else it's nothing."

sections.title: Above wisdom: the thirteen attributes of mercy, the source of all delights, and the eternity of Atik Yomin
sections.summary: Above wisdom, the thirteen attributes of mercy are the essential delight in the *gulgalta*, which can take delight in anything and forgives sin; and the three heads of *Atik* are the delight as it is in itself, before any will, the source of all delights. *Atik Yomin* means the eternity of the Essence as it shines into time: higher than time, it makes time infinite, as a line holds infinite points.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן הארת י''ג מדות הרחמים מלמעלה מחכמה שברצון כו',
שנושא עון וכו'
phrases.en: that He forgives sin.

blocks.text: But the light of the thirteen *middos harachamim* (attributes of mercy), above the *chachma* in the will, is the *etzem taanug* in the *gulgalta*. There Hashem can get *taanug* from anything, not *davka* according to the Torah. There is a revelation of G-d also in an *aveira* (a sin): our connection is expressed there too, just in a negative way. And so, **that He forgives sin.**

phrases.he: ומכל שכן מבחינת ג׳ ראשין דעתיק יומין שבלתי מלובש בנאצלים
phrases.en: and how much more so when we connect to the *gimmel reishin* of *Atik Yomin*, that it's not at all clothed in *ne'etzalim*,

phrases.he: והוא בחינת העונג כמו שהוא בעצמו
שעדיין לא נולד ממנו רצון כלל,
phrases.en: This is just the *etzem taanug* before it's related to anything outside, which makes a *ratzon*.

phrases.he: רק עתיד להיות ממנו כל רצון כו'
phrases.en: which is the *makor* which causes every *ratzon*.

blocks.text: **And how much more so when we connect to the gimmel reishin of Atik Yomin, that it's not at all clothed in ne'etzalim.** There it is just the essential connection to the Yidden, beyond anything we do or do not do: the delight as it is in itself, from which no will has yet been born. It is **just the etzem taanug before it's related to anything outside, which makes a ratzon**, **which is the makor** (source) **which causes every ratzon**: like the *yechida* (the essence of the soul) of a Jew, connected to G-d in essence.

phrases.he: והוא נחשב מעצמות התענוג הפשוט הכללי
שהוא מבחינת מקור כל התענוגים שבעצמות אור אין סוף
כמו שכתוב כי עמך מקור חיים,
phrases.en: "With You is the source of life,"

phrases.he: מקור כל התענוגים שברצון קדום כו'
phrases.en: this is the source of everything that comes in the *ratzon kadum*,

phrases.he: ונקרא עתיקא דעתיקין בכללות הכל כו'
phrases.en: it's called *Atik* of all *Atik*'s,

blocks.text: It counts as the essence of the simple, general delight, the source of all the delights in the *Atzmus Ein Sof*; in a person, it is like the soul before it comes in at all. As it says, **"With You is the source of life"**: **this is the source of everything that comes in the ratzon kadum.** And *Atika d'Atikin*: **it's called Atik of all Atik's**, all of it hidden.

phrases.he: ונקרא עתיק יומין כמו שכתוב בדניאל, ועתיק יומין יתיב כו',
phrases.en: And in general, pleasure is called *Atik Yomin*... "The Ancient of Days sat."

phrases.he: מלשון זקנה
phrases.en: means old age,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת נצחיות דעצמיות אור אין סוף
כשבא ומאיר למטה בהשתלשלות דקו וחוט כו'
phrases.en: when it comes into time, it becomes infinite.

blocks.text: **In general, pleasure is called Atik Yomin**, as Daniel says, **"The Ancient of Days sat."** *Mi'lashon zikna*: it **means old age**, the eternity of the *Atzmus Ein Sof*. The *Atzmus Ein Sof* is beyond change, and change is time. Being beyond all forms and change, it can come into anything and stays no matter what changes; that is the eternity of the *etzem*. It is higher than time, but **when it comes into time, it becomes infinite.**

phrases.he: אבל בעצמותו ממש, מי איכא זקנה קמי קודשא בריך הוא כו'
phrases.en: is there any age? How can you say that He's old?

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין ועד בחלופי אתוון דאחד
phrases.en: That *va'ed*, forever, eternal, is like a *chiluf* of *echad*,

phrases.he: פשוט עצמו

blocks.text: But in His Essence itself, before the Holy One, blessed be He, **is there any age? How can you say that He's old?** It is above time. As explained elsewhere, *va'ed* is an exchange of the letters of *echad*: **that va'ed, forever, eternal, is like a chiluf** (an exchange) **of echad**. Hashem's unity is beyond any division, so the *etzem* is higher than everything, can come into anything, and no change in time affects it: it is infinite.

phrases.he: שעצמות אור אין סוף שלמעלה מן הזמן דימי קדם כו',
כשמאיר בזמן, אז הזמן גם כן נצחי
phrases.en: So then the time itself becomes infinite.

phrases.he: כו' ואז נקרא עתיק יומין
phrases.en: then it's called *Atik Yomin*,

phrases.he: כו' ודי למבין:

blocks.text: When the *Atzmus Ein Sof*, above time, shines into time, time too is eternal: **so then the time itself becomes infinite.** Normally something made of finite parts, as time is made of seconds, hours, days and years, cannot go on forever.

blocks.title: Cheerios in a row
blocks.text: Take a bunch of Cheerios, start putting them next to each other, and keep adding: you will never get to an infinity. However big the number, finite parts relative to an infinity are all like zeros, and adding zeros never gets anywhere. From a finite power you cannot build up something infinite.

blocks.title: Points and a line
blocks.text: But in geometry, points have no space; they are zero-dimensional. Put a bunch of points next to each other and you will never get a line, not even a line segment, any length at all: "they're zeros." But a line automatically holds infinite points; that is how they define a line, an infinite series of points. It is higher than the whole matter of points, and therefore when it comes in, it makes it infinite.

blocks.title: Can time be infinite?
blocks.text: So really it is impossible to have time be infinite, as they discuss in *chakira* (philosophical inquiry), and the *Tzemach Tzedek* a little. But "it's not really true, really you can have infinite time": the Rebbe treats it in a *sicha* (a talk) as a *mah nafshach* (an either-way argument). From human intellect and the world's limitations, infinite time is impossible, so the world must have started at a certain time. And if it is infinite, it comes from a miraculous higher reality, and again there is a G-d who made it. Here he says the actual reality: it comes into time and makes it eternal.

And when it comes in, **it's called Atik Yomin**, from old age, because the *middos* of *Atik* are called *Atik Yomin*. The *etzem* of *Atik* is just plain *Atik*: totally removed, not infinite time, infinite *yomin* (days), just separate. *Atik Yomin* already relates to *Beriya*, creation: Hashem already gets a *taanug*, there is G-dliness within creation, and it makes the creation itself G-dly and infinite. And this is enough for one who understands.

reviewQuestions.question: If the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* is removed even from the simple delight, why did the early Kabbalists say that nothing is higher than pleasure?
What does the delight in winning, down to the victory dance and the paraphernalia, show about the *taanug pashut*, and what does it mean to be a fan of G-d?
How can the *Keser* be enclothed in every *sefira* and also encompass them all? What do the oil, the ten pits and the garments show?
Why is *Atik Yomin* still counted as the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*, and what does the drawing of a tree have to do with it?
Why will a father at his son's wedding grant anything, even turn judgment into kindness, and what level of the will does that reach?
Why did the early Kabbalists call *chachma* judgment, and how does that explain the many exact laws of the Torah?
